newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Rebels declare unlilateral ceasefire in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Rebels declare unlilateral ceasefire in Zaire.

text.p: The leader of rebel forces in eastern Zaire said he was calling a three-week unilateral ceasefire from 5 p.m. (1500 GMT) on Monday to allow refugees to leave for home.
But Laurent Kabila, head of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, said combat would resume if Zairean troops failed to respect the rebel ceasefire.

"The Alliance for Democracy following a unilateral decision will have a ceasefire to start at 5 p.m. today for three weeks," Kabila said in a telephone call to a correspondent for Voice of America radio in the Burundian capital Bujumbura.
"This is because of the disquiet of the international community, to allow the International Red Cross to evacuate the refugees who want to return to their original countries," he added.

"We hope that the unilateral ceasefire will be respected by the Zairean side. If they are against this decision, then combat will restart immediately," added Kabila, who said he was speaking from the rebel-held eastern Zairean city of Bukavu. He said both Bukavu and Goma city to the north were quiet.

The last international aid workers in eastern Zaire left on Saturday, leaving behind more than one million Rwandan and Burundian refugees and tens of thousands of Zaireans displaced by two weeks of fighting.
